```{r setup}
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What to set for a report
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

# The path to the config file, whose financialreport section names the
# combined Silver layer:
#
#   FINCOMMONS_CONFIG=/path/to/paths.yaml quarto render financialreport-comparison-report.qmd
#
# The financial year compared is taken from FINCOMMONS_YEAR where that is set.
# Otherwise it is the latest year in which at least two regimes hold
# `min_companies` companies each, since a comparison of one regime with
# nothing is not one.
config_path <- Sys.getenv("FINCOMMONS_CONFIG", "paths.yaml")
year_asked <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(Sys.getenv("FINCOMMONS_YEAR", "")))
min_companies <- 10

# How many financial years the chart of medians goes back from the year
# compared, and how many companies a regime needs in a year for its median of
# that year to be drawn at all.
n_years <- 8
min_for_median <- 10

# The point size of the text in a chart.
chart_base_size <- 9

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What the report counts as what
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

regimes <- c(esef = "ESEF", sec = "SEC", edinet = "EDINET")
frameworks <- c("IFRS", "US-GAAP", "JP-GAAP")

# The forms of an annual report, as in the coverage report beside this one
# and the sector factsheet of the esef module. A quarter's result over a
# year's equity is not a return.
annual_forms <- c("10-K", "10-K/A", "20-F", "20-F/A", "40-F", "40-F/A",
                  "120", "130")

# The measures compared, and the ratios taken of them. Every ratio is of two
# figures of the same report, so no currency is converted and none needs to
# be: a margin in yen is a margin in euro.
measures_used <- c("revenue", "profit_loss",
                   "profit_loss_attributable_to_parent", "assets", "equity")

# Banks and insurers, found from their own statements: a filer whose report
# carries a line only a bank or an insurer presents is one, under any of the
# three frameworks. Their revenue is interest or premium income and their
# balance sheet is the business, so a margin or an equity ratio of theirs is
# a different quantity from a company's and is left out of every figure. The
# IFRS and US-GAAP lines are those of the esef sector factsheet and the
# country quality factsheet; a Japanese bank, insurer or securities firm
# tags the industry elements of the financial statements taxonomy, whose
# names end in BNK, INS and SEC.
financial_concepts <- c(
  "ifrs-full:InterestRevenueCalculatedUsingEffectiveInterestMethod",
  "ifrs-full:InsuranceRevenue",
  "ifrs-full:InsuranceContractLiabilities",
  "ifrs-full:InsuranceServiceResult",
  "ifrs-full:InsuranceServiceExpenses",
  "ifrs-full:LoansAndAdvancesToBanks",
  "ifrs-full:DepositsFromCustomers",
  "us-gaap:InterestAndDividendIncomeOperating",
  "us-gaap:InterestIncomeExpenseNet",
  "us-gaap:InterestAndFeeIncomeLoansAndLeases",
  "us-gaap:PremiumsEarnedNet",
  "us-gaap:PolicyholderBenefitsAndClaimsIncurredNet",
  "us-gaap:LoansAndLeasesReceivableNetReportedAmount")
japanese_financial_suffix <- "(BNK|INS|SEC)$"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The design and the libraries
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(ggplot2)
design_file <- "r-corporate-design-functions-ggplot2.R"
design_path <- c(design_file, file.path("..", "..", "..", "templates", design_file))
design_path <- design_path[file.exists(design_path)]
if (length(design_path) == 0) {
  stop("The corporate design script ", design_file, " is neither beside this ",
       "template nor in the templates directory of the package.")
}
source(design_path[1])

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(yaml)
library(arrow)

if (!grepl("UTF-8", Sys.getlocale("LC_CTYPE"), ignore.case = TRUE)) {
  stop("The session does not run in a UTF-8 locale, so the names of issuers ",
       "and the typographic characters of this report would print as ",
       "<U+00B7> escapes. Render with LANG=en_US.UTF-8.")
}

period_year <- function(date) {
  y <- as.integer(format(date, "%Y"))
  ifelse(as.integer(format(date, "%m")) <= 6L, y - 1L, y)
}

catalogue_file <- "financialreport_measures.csv"
catalogue_path <- c(catalogue_file,
                    file.path("..", "..", "..", "data", catalogue_file))
catalogue_path <- catalogue_path[file.exists(catalogue_path)]
if (length(catalogue_path) == 0) {
  stop("The catalogue of measures ", catalogue_file, " is neither beside ",
       "this template nor in the data directory of the package.")
}
catalogue <- read.csv(catalogue_path[1], stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                      encoding = "UTF-8") %>%
  as_tibble()

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The Silver layer
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

yaml_paths <- read_yaml(config_path)
path_silver <- yaml_paths[["financialreport"]][["silver"]]
if (is.list(path_silver)) path_silver <- path_silver[["path"]]
if (is.null(path_silver)) {
  stop("The config file ", config_path, " names no Silver layer for ",
       "financialreport.")
}
for (table in c("fact", "filing")) {
  if (!dir.exists(file.path(path_silver, table))) {
    stop("The combined Silver layer in ", path_silver, " has no ", table,
         " table. Build it with fincommons.financialreport.combined.",
         "update_silver_financialreport.")
  }
  if (dir.exists(file.path(path_silver, table, "_delta_log"))) {
    stop("The ", table, " table of the combined module is a Delta table, ",
         "which this template does not read. Write the Silver layer as ",
         "parquet, or read the table through Spark.")
  }
}

annual <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "filing")) %>%
  filter(facts > 0) %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate(source = as.character(source),
         fy = period_year(period_end),
         issuer = paste0(coalesce(lei, ""), "|", coalesce(cik, ""), "|",
                         coalesce(edinet_code, ""))) %>%
  filter(source == "esef" | form %in% annual_forms, !is.na(fy),
         !is.na(framework))

# Investment funds, which file their annual reports with the agency under
# the document type of a company's; see the coverage report beside this one.
edinet_ids <- annual$filing[annual$source == "edinet"]
fund_ids <- if (length(edinet_ids) == 0) character(0) else
  open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "fact")) %>%
    filter(source == "edinet", filing %in% edinet_ids,
           grepl("^jpsps", concept) | grepl("FND$", concept)) %>%
    distinct(filing) %>% collect() %>% pull(filing)

# Banks and insurers, by issuer: an issuer that ever presented one of their
# lines is one in every year, so that a bank does not move into the
# population of companies in a year whose report happened to tag less.
financial_issuers <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "fact")) %>%
  filter(concept %in% financial_concepts |
           (source == "edinet" & grepl(japanese_financial_suffix, concept))) %>%
  distinct(lei, cik, edinet_code) %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate(issuer = paste0(coalesce(lei, ""), "|", coalesce(cik, ""), "|",
                         coalesce(edinet_code, ""))) %>%
  pull(issuer) %>% unique()

annual <- annual %>%
  mutate(fund = filing %in% fund_ids,
         financial = issuer %in% financial_issuers)
companies_all <- annual %>% filter(!fund, !financial)

# The measures of each report: the group's figure for the report's own year,
# or the parent company's own where a Japanese filer prepares no group
# accounts; under the framework of the filing, since a Japanese group
# reporting under IFRS states its parent's accounts under Japan GAAP too.
basis_members <- c("NonConsolidatedMember")
values <- open_dataset(file.path(path_silver, "fact")) %>%
  filter(measure %in% measures_used, !is.na(value), prd_end == period_end,
         is.na(dimensions) | dimensions %in% basis_members) %>%
  select(source, filing, framework, measure, dimensions, value) %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate(source = as.character(source)) %>%
  semi_join(companies_all, by = c("source", "filing", "framework")) %>%
  arrange(source, filing, measure, !is.na(dimensions)) %>%
  distinct(source, filing, measure, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(source, filing, measure, value) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = value)
for (key in setdiff(measures_used, names(values))) values[[key]] <- NA_real_

# One report per company and year: the one stating most of the measures, and
# between equals the latest filing by its identifier, so that an amendment
# that restates the year wins over the report it amends and the choice is
# the same on every run.
companies <- companies_all %>%
  inner_join(values, by = c("source", "filing")) %>%
  mutate(filled = rowSums(!is.na(across(all_of(measures_used))))) %>%
  arrange(source, issuer, fy, desc(filled), desc(filing)) %>%
  distinct(source, issuer, fy, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    # The total result where it is stated and the parent's share where it is
    # not; the coverage report shows why neither alone reaches both regimes.
    profit = coalesce(profit_loss, profit_loss_attributable_to_parent),
    profit_basis = ifelse(!is.na(profit_loss), "total", "parent"),
    net_margin = ifelse(!is.na(revenue) & revenue > 0, profit / revenue * 100, NA),
    equity_ratio = ifelse(!is.na(assets) & assets > 0, equity / assets * 100, NA),
    roe = ifelse(!is.na(equity) & equity > 0, profit / equity * 100, NA),
    loss = profit < 0,
    regime = factor(unname(regimes[source]), levels = unname(regimes)))

counts_by_year <- companies %>% count(source, fy)
eligible <- counts_by_year %>%
  filter(n >= min_companies) %>%
  count(fy, name = "regimes") %>%
  filter(regimes >= 2)
report_year <- if (!is.na(year_asked)) year_asked else
  if (nrow(eligible) > 0) max(eligible$fy) else max(companies$fy)
year_rows <- companies %>% filter(fy == report_year)
if (nrow(year_rows) == 0) {
  stop("The combined tables hold no annual report of a company for the ",
       "financial year ", report_year, ".")
}
regimes_in_year <- intersect(names(regimes), unique(year_rows$source))
```

```{r title, results='asis'}
# The title of the document, which a screen reader announces and without
# which typst refuses to write a PDF/UA document.
typst_document_title(paste0("Companies across regimes: ",
                            paste(regimes[regimes_in_year], collapse = ", "),
                            ", financial year ", report_year))
```

```{r formats}
fmt <- function(x, digits = 0) {
  x <- ifelse(!is.na(x) & abs(x) < 0.5 / 10^digits, 0, x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "–",
         formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",",
                 decimal.mark = "."))
}
wrap_caption <- function(text, width = 125) {
  paste(strwrap(text, width = width), collapse = "\n")
}
source_caption <- caption_corporate_design(
  source = paste("filings.xbrl.org, SEC EDGAR, EDINET;",
                 "the combined tables of fincommons.financialreport."),
  lang = "en")
# It is named apart from typst_string of the design script, which also puts
# the quotes around the text and which the title of the document and its
# coloured tables call: a function of the same name here would replace it.
typst_escape <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("\\\\", "\\\\\\\\", x)
  gsub("\"", "\\\\\"", x)
}
ts <- function(x) {
  x <- ifelse(is.na(x), "–", as.character(x))
  paste0("\"", typst_escape(x), "\"")
}
typst_table <- function(df, widths, align, size = 7.5) {
  cells <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(df)), function(i) {
    paste(ts(unlist(df[i, ], use.names = FALSE)), collapse = ", ")
  }, character(1))
  paste0(
    "\n```{=typst}\n#block(width: 100%, text(size: ", size, "pt, {\n",
    "set par(justify: false)\ntable(\n",
    "  columns: (", paste(widths, collapse = ", "), "),\n",
    "  align: (", paste(align, collapse = ", "), "),\n",
    "  inset: (x: 4pt, y: 2.8pt),\n",
    "  stroke: (x, y) => if y == 0 { (top: 0.7pt + rgb(\"#22282E\"), ",
    "bottom: 0.4pt + rgb(\"#22282E\")) } else { none },\n",
    "  table.header(", paste0("text(weight: \"bold\", ", ts(names(df)), ")",
                             collapse = ", "), "),\n  ",
    paste(cells, collapse = ",\n  "),
    ",\n  table.hline(stroke: 0.7pt + rgb(\"#22282E\"))\n)}))\n```\n\n")
}
breakable <- function(x) gsub("([a-z])([A-Z])", "\\1\u200b\\2", x, perl = TRUE)

cols <- design_colours()
# The colours of the regimes are the first three of the accessible palette of
# the design, which stay apart for a reader who does not see red or green;
# the coverage report beside this one uses the same three. No chart tells the
# regimes apart by colour alone: the box plots name them on their axis, and
# the lines over time differ by line type and point shape as well.
regime_colours <- setNames(palette_accessible[1:3], c("ESEF", "SEC", "EDINET"))
regime_shapes <- c("ESEF" = 16, "SEC" = 17, "EDINET" = 15)

# The median and the quartiles of a ratio, over the companies that state its
# two figures.
quart <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) return(c(n = 0, q1 = NA, med = NA, q3 = NA))
  q <- unname(quantile(x, c(.25, .5, .75), type = 7))
  c(n = length(x), q1 = q[1], med = q[2], q3 = q[3])
}
summarise_ratios <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    summarise(
      companies = n(),
      margin_n = quart(net_margin)[["n"]], margin = quart(net_margin)[["med"]],
      margin_q1 = quart(net_margin)[["q1"]], margin_q3 = quart(net_margin)[["q3"]],
      eqr_n = quart(equity_ratio)[["n"]], eqr = quart(equity_ratio)[["med"]],
      roe_n = quart(roe)[["n"]], roe = quart(roe)[["med"]],
      loss = mean(loss, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
      total_basis = mean(profit_basis[!is.na(profit)] == "total") * 100,
      .groups = "drop")
}
```

```{r cover, results='asis'}
title <- "Companies across regimes"
subtitle <- paste0("Margins, equity ratios and returns from the annual reports ",
                   "of ", paste(regimes[regimes_in_year], collapse = ", "),
                   ", financial year ", report_year)

tile <- function(value, label, colour) {
  paste0("box(width: 100%, inset: (x: 8pt, y: 7pt), stroke: (left: 2pt + rgb(\"",
         colour, "\")), [#text(size: 17pt, weight: \"bold\", ", ts(value),
         ")\\ #text(size: 7.5pt, fill: rgb(\"#5C666F\"), ", ts(label), ")])")
}
by_regime <- year_rows %>% group_by(source, regime) %>% summarise_ratios() %>%
  arrange(match(source, names(regimes)))

cat("```{=typst}\n")
cat("#set page(header: [#set text(size: 7pt, fill: rgb(\"#5C666F\"))\n",
    "  #grid(columns: (1fr, auto), [#text(weight: \"bold\", ",
    ts("Companies across regimes"), ") #h(6pt) #text(",
    ts(paste("Financial year", report_year)), ")], [#text(",
    ts(paste("Rendered on", format(Sys.Date(), "%d %B %Y"))), ")])\n",
    "  #v(-4pt) #line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.5pt + rgb(\"#DCE1E5\"))],\n",
    "  footer: [#set text(size: 7pt, fill: rgb(\"#5C666F\"))\n",
    "  #line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.5pt + rgb(\"#DCE1E5\")) #v(-2pt)\n",
    "  #grid(columns: (1fr, auto), [#text(",
    ts("Source: filings.xbrl.org, SEC EDGAR, EDINET; fincommons.financialreport. Not investment advice."),
    ")], [#context counter(page).display()])],\n  numbering: \"1\")\n", sep = "")
cat("#text(size: 8pt, tracking: 1.6pt, fill: rgb(\"#5C666F\"), ",
    ts("COMPARISON REPORT · ESEF · SEC · EDINET"), ")\n", sep = "")
cat("#v(2pt)\n#line(length: 100%, stroke: 1.2pt + rgb(\"#C10016\"))\n#v(8pt)\n")
cat("#text(size: 21pt, weight: \"bold\", ", ts(title), ")\n#v(1pt)\n", sep = "")
cat("#text(size: 10pt, fill: rgb(\"#5C666F\"), ", ts(subtitle), ")\n#v(10pt)\n", sep = "")
tiles <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(by_regime)), function(i) {
  r <- by_regime[i, ]
  tile(paste0(fmt(r$margin, 1), " %"),
       paste0("median net margin, ", r$regime, ", of ", fmt(r$margin_n),
              " companies stating revenue"),
       regime_colours[[as.character(r$regime)]])
}, character(1))
cat("#grid(columns: (", paste(rep("1fr", length(tiles)), collapse = ", "),
    "), column-gutter: 8pt,\n  ", paste(tiles, collapse = ",\n  "),
    "\n)\n#v(8pt)\n", sep = "")
cat("```\n\n")

lines <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(by_regime)), function(i) {
  r <- by_regime[i, ]
  paste0("**", r$regime, "**: ", fmt(r$companies), " companies; a median net ",
         "margin of ", fmt(r$margin, 1), " %, an equity ratio of ",
         fmt(r$eqr, 1), " % and a return on equity of ", fmt(r$roe, 1),
         " %; ", fmt(r$loss), " % made a loss.")
}, character(1))
cat("Every figure on these pages is a ratio of two figures of one annual ",
    "report, so nothing is converted between currencies. Banks, insurers and ",
    "investment funds are left out, since their margins and equity ratios ",
    "are different quantities, and the populations are whatever each regime's ",
    "part of the lake holds -- not samples of the same economy. A difference ",
    "between the regimes is a difference between those populations and ",
    "between what their frameworks count before it is anything else.\n\n",
    sep = "")
cat(paste0("- ", lines, collapse = "\n"), "\n\n")
```

## The year compared

```{r year-table, results='asis'}
temp <- year_rows %>%
  group_by(source, regime, framework) %>%
  summarise_ratios() %>%
  arrange(match(source, names(regimes)), match(framework, frameworks)) %>%
  transmute(Regime = as.character(regime), Framework = framework,
            Companies = fmt(companies),
            `Net margin, %` = fmt(margin, 1),
            `Quartiles, %` = ifelse(is.na(margin_q1), "–",
                                    paste0(fmt(margin_q1, 1), " to ",
                                           fmt(margin_q3, 1))),
            `Equity ratio, %` = fmt(eqr, 1),
            `ROE, %` = fmt(roe, 1),
            `With a loss, %` = fmt(loss),
            `Result as total, %` = fmt(total_basis))
cat(typst_table(temp, widths = c("auto", "auto", "1fr", rep("auto", 6)),
                align = c("left", "left", rep("right", 7))))
cat("Medians over the companies whose report states both figures of a ratio. ",
    "Net margin is the result over revenue; the equity ratio is equity over ",
    "total assets, both at the year end; the return on equity is the result ",
    "over year-end equity, for companies whose equity is positive. The ",
    "result is the total, including non-controlling interests, where the ",
    "report states it and the parent's share where it does not; the last ",
    "column says how often it was the total. A framework is the one a ",
    "report's concepts belong to: the IFRS row of the SEC is the foreign ",
    "issuers filing with the Commission under IFRS.\n\n", sep = "")
```

```{r year-chart-data}
limits <- c(net_margin = 60, equity_ratio = 100, roe = 80)
temp <- year_rows %>%
  select(regime, net_margin, equity_ratio, roe) %>%
  pivot_longer(-regime, names_to = "ratio", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  mutate(clipped = pmax(pmin(value, limits[ratio]), -limits[ratio]),
         ratio = factor(ratio, levels = names(limits),
                        labels = c("Net margin, %", "Equity ratio, %",
                                   "Return on equity, %")),
         regime = factor(regime, levels = rev(unname(regimes))))

# What the chart shows, as text for its alt text: for each ratio, each
# regime's companies, median and quartiles.
spread_text <- temp %>%
  group_by(ratio, regime) %>%
  summarise(text = paste0(as.character(regime[1]), " ", fmt(n()), " companies, median ",
                          fmt(median(value), 1), ", quartiles ",
                          fmt(quantile(value, .25), 1), " to ",
                          fmt(quantile(value, .75), 1)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(ratio, desc(regime)) %>%
  group_by(ratio) %>%
  summarise(text = paste0(ratio[1], ": ", paste(text, collapse = "; ")),
            .groups = "drop")
alt_year <- if (nrow(temp) == 0) {
  paste0("Box plots of the ratios of ", report_year, ", which are empty: no ",
         "company states the figures of a ratio.")
} else {
  paste0("Box plots in three panels, net margin, equity ratio and return on ",
         "equity in per cent, one row per regime named on the axis, with every ",
         "company of ", report_year, " as a point; values beyond ",
         paste0(limits, collapse = ", "), " per cent in the three panels are ",
         "drawn at the edge. ", paste(spread_text$text, collapse = ". "), ".")
}
```

         "interquartile range, and values beyond the scale are drawn at its edge"),
         110),
       caption = wrap_caption(source_caption)) +
  theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size, grid = "x",
                         axis.title = element_blank())

## Over time

```{r trend-data}
years <- seq(report_year - n_years + 1, report_year)
temp <- companies %>%
  filter(fy %in% years) %>%
  group_by(regime, fy) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            `Net margin, %` = median(net_margin, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Equity ratio, %` = median(equity_ratio, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Return on equity, %` = median(roe, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n >= min_for_median) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(regime, fy, n), names_to = "ratio", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(ratio = factor(ratio, levels = c("Net margin, %", "Equity ratio, %",
                                          "Return on equity, %")))

# What the chart shows, as text for its alt text: each regime's median of
# each ratio in its first and its last year charted, with its highest and
# lowest year.
trend_text <- temp %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  arrange(ratio, regime, fy) %>%
  group_by(ratio, regime) %>%
  summarise(text = paste0(as.character(regime[1]), " ", fmt(value[1], 1), " in ", fy[1],
                          if (n() > 1) paste0(" and ", fmt(value[n()], 1), " in ", fy[n()]) else "",
                          if (n() > 2) paste0(", highest ", fmt(max(value), 1), " in ",
                                              fy[which.max(value)], ", lowest ",
                                              fmt(min(value), 1), " in ",
                                              fy[which.min(value)]) else ""),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(ratio) %>%
  summarise(text = paste0(ratio[1], ": ", paste(text, collapse = "; ")),
            .groups = "drop")
alt_trend <- if (nrow(trend_text) == 0) {
  paste0("Line chart of the medians by financial year, which is empty: no ",
         "regime holds ", min_for_median, " companies in any year from ",
         min(years), " to ", max(years), ".")
} else {
  paste0("Line chart in three panels of the median net margin, equity ratio ",
         "and return on equity in per cent by financial year, ", min(years),
         " to ", max(years), ", one line per regime told apart by colour, line ",
         "type and point shape, drawn where a regime holds at least ",
         min_for_median, " companies in the year. ",
         paste(trend_text$text, collapse = ". "), ".")
}
```

```{r trend}
#| fig-height: 2.8
#| fig-alt: !expr alt_trend
ggplot(temp, aes(x = fy, y = value, colour = regime, linetype = regime,
                 shape = regime)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 1.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = regime_colours, name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = setNames(linetypes_accessible[1:3], names(regime_colours)),
                        name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = regime_shapes, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = function(l) seq(ceiling(l[1]), floor(l[2]), by = 2)) +
  facet_wrap(~ratio, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(subtitle = wrap_caption(paste0(
         "Medians by financial year, where a regime holds at least ",
         min_for_median, " companies in the year"), 110),
       caption = wrap_caption(source_caption)) +
  theme_corporate_design(base_size = chart_base_size, grid = "y",
                         axis.title = element_blank()) +
  theme(legend.key.width = grid::unit(2.2, "lines"))
```

```{r trend-note, results='asis'}
spans <- companies %>%
  group_by(regime) %>%
  summarise(from = min(fy), to = max(fy),
            per_year = round(median(table(fy))), .groups = "drop")
cat("The regimes do not cover the same years: ",
    paste0(spans$regime, " from ", spans$from, " to ", spans$to,
           " (some ", fmt(spans$per_year), " companies a year)",
           collapse = ", "),
    ". A line is the same population of filers only as far as the lake ",
    "collected the same filers each year, and the latest year of a regime ",
    "can be one still being filed.\n\n", sep = "")
```

## IFRS in three regimes

```{r ifrs, results='asis'}
temp <- year_rows %>%
  filter(framework == "IFRS") %>%
  group_by(source, regime) %>%
  summarise_ratios() %>%
  arrange(match(source, names(regimes)))
if (nrow(temp) >= 2) {
  cat("The one framework all three regimes share. A European issuer files ",
      "its consolidated accounts under IFRS by law; a foreign issuer may file ",
      "with the Commission under IFRS rather than US GAAP; and a Japanese ",
      "group may adopt IFRS voluntarily and tag it against Japan's own IFRS ",
      "taxonomy. The concepts differ by regime and the catalogue of measures ",
      "takes them to be the same figures, so these rows compare companies ",
      "rather than frameworks.\n\n", sep = "")
  cat(typst_table(temp %>% transmute(
        Regime = as.character(regime), Companies = fmt(companies),
        `Net margin, %` = fmt(margin, 1), `Equity ratio, %` = fmt(eqr, 1),
        `ROE, %` = fmt(roe, 1), `With a loss, %` = fmt(loss)),
      widths = c("1fr", rep("auto", 5)), align = c("left", rep("right", 5))))
  small <- temp %>% filter(companies < min_companies)
  if (nrow(small) > 0) {
    cat("Too few to read a median from: ",
        paste0(small$regime, " (", fmt(small$companies), ")", collapse = ", "),
        ".\n\n", sep = "")
  }
} else {
  cat("Only one regime holds companies reporting under IFRS in ", report_year,
      ", so there is nothing to set beside it.\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

## What the figures do not share

```{r caveats, results='asis'}
used <- catalogue %>%
  filter(measure %in% measures_used, nzchar(caveat)) %>%
  group_by(caveat) %>%
  summarise(where = paste0(unique(paste0(measure, ", ", framework, " (",
                                         element, ")")), collapse = "; "),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(where)
cat("The catalogue of measures takes concepts of three frameworks to be the ",
    "same figure, and says where they are not quite. These are its caveats ",
    "on the measures this report uses, as the README of the combined module ",
    "asks of anyone publishing a comparison across regimes.\n\n", sep = "")
cat(typst_table(used %>% transmute(`Where` = breakable(where), Caveat = caveat),
                widths = c("4.4cm", "1fr"), align = c("left", "left"),
                size = 6.8))
```

## How to read this report

```{r notes, results='asis'}
n_funds <- sum(annual$fund & annual$fy == report_year)
n_financial <- n_distinct(annual$issuer[annual$financial & !annual$fund &
                                          annual$fy == report_year])
notes <- c(
  paste0("**What it reads.** The tables *filing* and *fact* of ",
         "`fincommons.financialreport.combined`, and the materialised ",
         "measures of the fact table: a figure counts where the report tags ",
         "the concept the catalogue ranks first for its framework, for the ",
         "entity as a whole and for the report's own year. A Japanese filer ",
         "that prepares no group accounts is read from its own, which it ",
         "states under `NonConsolidatedMember`."),
  paste0("**Which reports.** Annual reports only -- every ESEF filing, the ",
         "forms 10-K, 20-F and 40-F with the Commission and the document ",
         "types 120 and 130 with the agency -- and one per company and year, ",
         "the one that states most of the measures. Left out of ", report_year,
         ": ", fmt(n_financial), " banks and insurers, found from the lines ",
         "their own reports present, and ", fmt(n_funds), " annual reports ",
         "of Japanese investment funds."),
  paste0("**Which year.** A financial year is the calendar year it mostly ",
         "falls in: a year ending on or before 30 June counts as the year ",
         "before, so a Japanese year to 31 March 2026 is 2025.",
         if (is.na(year_asked)) paste0(" ", report_year, " is the latest ",
           "year in which at least two regimes hold ", min_companies,
           " companies; FINCOMMONS_YEAR chooses another.") else ""),
  paste0("**What it does not say.** The populations are what the lake ",
         "collected, not samples drawn alike: the ESEF part holds the ",
         "countries collected, the SEC part the registrants named, the EDINET ",
         "part the weeks of indexes read. A median that differs between the ",
         "regimes may say more about which companies each part holds than ",
         "about the regimes. The coverage report beside this one says what ",
         "each part holds."),
  paste0("This report is produced by a template of the open-source project ",
         "fincommons. It reads public records, is given without warranty as ",
         "to correctness or completeness, carries no association with the ",
         "issuers, the repository, the Commission or the agency, and is not ",
         "investment advice."))
cat(paste(notes, collapse = "\n\n"))
```
